summary: Discovery call to evaluate Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for embeddings and reranking. Acme is running hybrid search (BM25 + vectors) and wants to reduce latency for reranking while controlling costs. Main concerns: throughput (500+ QPS peak), embedding dimensionality (256 vs 768 vs 1536), integration with existing vector DBs, and VPC/on-prem security requirements.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Header: 2025-01-28 15:00 PST | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jill Thompson (Acme Head of Search), Carlos Mendez (Acme ML Eng), Priya Sharma (Acme CTO)

Summary: Quick discovery to understand Acme's current reranking pipeline, volumes, and security needs. Focus on embedding dimensionality, vector DB choice, throughput needs, and where Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private fit.

00:00:03 Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Real quick intros?
00:00:08 Jill: Jill here, I run search and relevance at Acme, been looking at ways to speed up reranking for our product search.
00:00:15 Carlos: Carlos, ML infra, I own the embedding pipeline and vector infra. We're using Pinecone today for production, some experiments with Milvus.
00:00:21 Priya: Priya, CTO. Interested in the security and cost implications — especially for peak season.
00:00:27 Samir: Samir from Redwood, infra and perf. We'll try to get a clear perf baseline and discuss options (hosted, dedicated, private).
00:00:33 Morgan: Great. Jill, can you describe the current reranking workflow and what you want to improve?
00:00:40 Jill: Sure. Right now we do BM25 to get top 200 documents, then a re-rank model that uses cross-encoder style scoring with context and 768-dim embeddings for a hybrid approach. We saw latency spikes during promotions — tail latency is a pain. Also cost of reranking at scale is non-trivial. We're serving around 300 QPS average, peaks at 800 QPS during big promos. Our objective is <150ms p95 on rerank stage and to cut inference cost by ~30%.
00:01:12 Carlos: To add, our embeddings are 768 dims from an in-house transformer. Vector DB is Pinecone; we also keep a Redis cache for hot queries. The reranker currently calls a GPU model for cross-encoder scoring for the top 20 results.
00:01:25 Samir: Ok that's helpful. Do you do offline pre-computed embeddings for docs or compute on the fly?
00:01:30 Carlos: Docs are precomputed and stored in Pinecone; user queries we embed at request time. Average doc vector size ~2KB, index size ~120M vectors.
00:01:40 Morgan: Thanks. So the core questions are throughput for embeddings + reranking, vector DB integrations, and options for private networking / compliance, right?
00:01:48 Jill: Yes. And behavior of mixed strategies — using Hosted for embeddings but Dedicated for reranking, or going full Private. We need options that let us test quickly but scale to enterprise.
00:01:58 Samir: Quick note on terminology: when I say Hosted I mean the Redwood API (multi-tenant) with standard SLA, Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for a single customer, and Private is customer-controlled control plane (VPC or on-prem). Each has tradeoffs on latency, cost, and data residency.
00:02:12 Priya: Security-wise we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, and KMS integration. For some data domains we'd like to keep embeddings entirely in our VPC. So Private or Dedicated with VPC peering is interesting.
00:02:25 Samir: We support SSO, KMS/HSM integration for Dedicated/Private and can provide SOC2 docs. For Private we can provide an on-prem package. I'll share the security whitepaper and KMS integration notes after the call.
00:02:36 Jill: Awesome. Now on the embedding dims, Carlos — have you considered 256-dim vectors? They reduce index size and cost but may impact quality. We're exploring 256 -> 768 tradeoffs.
00:02:47 Carlos: We tried 256 in a small A/B and saw a hit on edge cases. Main consumer-facing queries lost relevance for long-tail queries. We need to quantify for our dataset.
00:02:56 Samir: For throughput, embedding dimension affects memory and throughput. On Redwood Dedicated we can choose quantization profiles; 768 with int8/4-bit quantization often gets close to 256 float memory footprint but preserves quality. Also continuous batching and KV cache help lower per-token cost and latency for repeated prefixes.
00:03:16 Morgan: Can you elaborate on hybrid search? How do you see BM25 + vector rerank working with Redwood?
00:03:22 Samir: Two patterns we see: 1) BM25 to narrow to top N then vector re-rank using embeddings similarity plus a cross-encoder for final score, or 2) approximate nearest neighbor search for a larger candidate set then rerank. For Acme, BM25->top200->embedding rerank->cross-encoder for top20 matches what you described and fits well. The key is fast embedding lookup and low-latency reranker.
00:03:44 Jill: We're concerned about vector DB integration. If we keep Pinecone, can Redwood sit in front as the reranker?
00:03:50 Samir: Yes, you can keep Pinecone. Typical pattern: Pinecone for ANN and storage, Redwood for model inferencing (embeddings or reranker). Redwood can call Pinecone or you can push embeddings into Redwood cache for hot docs. We also have connectors and SDKs; integration is straightforward. The other option is to use Redwood's own cached embedding store on Dedicated/Private to reduce network hops.
00:04:10 Carlos: Latency numbers matter. For cross-encoder on GPU, what's realistic for p95 if we do batched reranking for top20?
00:04:18 Samir: On Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching, we've seen p95 around 60-120ms for 20-item cross-encoder rerank at 500 QPS with autoscaling and proper batching. Hosted multi-tenant might be slightly higher but still within 80-180ms depending on batchability. If you need strict 150ms p95, Dedicated is the safer bet.
00:04:43 Priya: What's the cost delta between Hosted vs Dedicated? Even a rough ballpark is useful.
00:04:49 Morgan: We'll follow up with numbers but generally Hosted is pay-as-you-go per request/token, Dedicated is capacity commit (monthly) which can be cheaper at scale but requires a commitment. We'll send example pricing slices.
00:04:59 Jill: Another operational question — peak promos can see burst to 800 QPS. What's the autoscaling/burst behavior on Dedicated?
00:05:07 Samir: Dedicated has reserved pools and configurable burst capacity; you can define autoscaling policies. For bursts we recommend a mix: keep a buffer of spare capacity and configured fallback policies (e.g., fall back to a lower-cost model variant or reduce rerank depth) if saturated. We can simulate promos with a stress test.
00:05:22 Carlos: For our current infra, network egress to Pinecone and to Redwood API will add overhead. If we move embeddings storage closer to Redwood (Private/Dedicated), do you have connectors for S3 or object stores for bulk ingest?
00:05:34 Samir: Yes, ingestion from S3 is supported. For Private we can deploy connectors in your VPC to access object stores without egress. For Dedicated we often stage embeddings in a co-located cache to avoid repeated external network calls.
00:05:46 Jill: About model variants — could we use a two-stage model: a cheaper 256-dim dense retriever to prune and a higher-quality 768/1536 cross-encoder for rerank? That would be a cost optimization path.
00:05:57 Samir: Absolutely. Many customers do a hierarchical approach: cheap first-stage retriever (dense or sparse) for candidate generation, then high-quality cross-encoder only on top-k. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/quantization profiles and suggest a model mix. We can run evals on your dev prompts to recommend dims and thresholds.
00:06:12 Carlos: Can Redwood host our embedding model or do we need to host it? We have a custom model and some licensing constraints.
00:06:19 Samir: Both are possible. Hosted can host open models; Dedicated/Private lets you bring your own model binary. For private licensing we can run the model inside your VPC or on-prem. If you need to keep model secrets on-prem, Private is recommended.
00:06:31 Priya: For compliance, we need audit logs for inference requests and per-token cost breakdown for chargeback. Is that in Redwood Console?
00:06:38 Morgan: Yes, Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We can enable audit log forwarding to your SIEM for Dedicated/Private.
00:06:48 Jill: Great. On the topic of reranking accuracy, can you run a small eval/human-in-the-loop test? We have a labeled dev set of 2k queries.
00:06:56 Samir: We can. Typical flow: you share the dev set, we run candidate generation and rerank with a few model variants (256/768 dims, different quantization), and return MRR/ndcg metrics plus latency/cost tradeoffs. That will help decide dimension and Dedicated vs Hosted.
00:07:10 Carlos: For the benchmark, what would you need from us? Data format? Baseline metrics?
00:07:15 Samir: We'll need sample queries, ground-truth relevance labels, a snapshot of the index (or a sampling of vectors), and baseline QPS targets. For the initial benchmark, 500 QPS sustained with peaks to 800 would be good. We'll run it against Dedicated and Hosted to compare.
00:07:29 Morgan: Let's talk timelines. Jill, you mentioned pilot before Q2?
00:07:32 Jill: Yes, we'd like to run a pilot in February and evaluate through March to be ready for Q2 promos.
00:07:37 Morgan: Ok good. We'll prioritize the benchmark so you can choose model dims. Samir, you'll run the bench and share results?
00:07:42 Samir: Yep. I'll set up a benchmark plan and propose dates this week.
00:07:46 Priya: One more question — we sometimes need private connectivity for GDPR-sensitive vectors. Does Redwood support VPC peering and private link?
00:07:53 Samir: Yes, Dedicated and Private support VPC peering and PrivateLink options. Private has full control-plane in your environment. We'll include a short architecture note.
00:08:03 Jill: Anything else from the team?
00:08:06 Carlos: Curious about embedding storage formats. Does Redwood support IVF/HNSW/OPQ variants and how that affects latency?
00:08:13 Samir: We support HNSW and PQ variants via connectors or in the integrated index depending on deployment. Index choice affects recall/latency tradeoffs. We'll include a short doc comparing index types for your dataset size.
00:08:26 Morgan: Okay let's move to recap and next steps.
00:08:30 Morgan: Recap — Acme needs: 1) benchmark for 500 QPS with peaks to 800, 2) evals for 256 vs 768 dims on your dev set, 3) security docs and options for Dedicated/Private with VPC peering, 4) pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated.
00:08:47 Jill: Correct. Also a short ops playbook for promo bursts and fallback policies.
00:08:53 Morgan: Action items captured. We'll send pricing and schedule the benchmark. Samir will own the bench; Morgan will send pricing/security docs. Carlos will share dataset samples.
00:09:03 Samir: I'll post a bench plan in a follow-up calendar invite and link to a shared S3 bucket for the dataset.
00:09:09 Jill: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the results.
00:09:13 Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
00:09:15 Morgan: Thanks all!
